```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(p8105.datasets)
data("ny_noaa")
view(ny_noaa)
```

## Problem 1: NY NOAA

### Load the data and describe it
`ny_noaa` data contain the daily weather observations from 747 New York weather stations from 1981 through 2010. There are 2,595,176 rows and 7 columns. Each row represents one station-day. The measured variables are `prcp`, `snow`, `snwd`, and `tmax`/`tmin`. Missingness is noticeable, especially for max/min temperatures (44% NA) and snow depth (23% NA). Addition to that, there are 15% of snowfall and 6% of precipitation missing. The missingness limits the comparisons between records from different years.

### Cleaning and check snowfall values
```{r}
noaa_clean =
  ny_noaa %>%
  mutate(
    date = as.Date(date),
    year = year(date),
    month = month(date),
    day = day(date),
    across(c(prcp, snow, snwd, tmax, tmin),
           ~ as.numeric(as.character(.x))),
    prcp = prcp / 10, 
    tmax = tmax / 10, 
    tmin = tmin / 10
  )

noaa_clean %>%
  count(snow, sort = TRUE) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5)
```

I created numeric year, month, and day variables from `date`. The data stores precipitation in tenths of a millimeter and temperatures in tenths of a degree Celsius, so I divided those columns by 10 to get the reasonable units. Snowfall and snow depth are already in millimeters so no change was made. 
0 mm is by far the most common snowfall value. The next most common values include 25, 13, and 51 mm. 0 is common because in most records there is no snowfall.

### two-panel plot for averaged Jan and July max t by station and year
```{r}
station_monthly_tmax =
  noaa_clean %>%
  filter(month %in% c(1, 7)) %>%
  group_by(id, year, month) %>%
  summarise(mean_tmax = mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(is.finite(mean_tmax)) %>%
  mutate(month = factor(month, 
                        labels = c("January", "July")))

ggplot(station_monthly_tmax,
       aes(x = year, y = mean_tmax, group = interaction(id, month))) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.2, linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_smooth(aes(group = month), se = FALSE) +
  facet_grid(. ~ month) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Mean daily maximum temperature (°C)",
       title = "Mean January and July max temperature by station")
```
The pplot is divided into two panel, separately represening January and July. In each panel, one line represents the record from one station. The blue line summarize the broad temporal pattern. January plot has much more variation. July temperatures are considerably higher and appear less variable across stations. Some station-year observations appear higher or lower than others (outliers) and may need further check.
